passage: Eight companies presented their solutions to NASA. To everyone's surprise, the company which won the contract for the Apollo suits wasn't as big as the others and owed its reputation to its product line of female underwear. The company came up with a softer and more flexible space suit made almost entirely of fabric. Each suit was made by seamstresses using their hands and sewing machines. Their skills were acquired from years of making women's underwear. What made the work so hard was the number of layers and components involved. In the end, each suit worn on the moon was comprised of some four thousand pieces of fabric and twenty-one layers of distinct materials, weighing 82 kg at the time. It remains the most complex space suit to have been used to date, and it was the fruit of the craftsmanship of the women skilled in sewing and making underwear, rather than NASA's technological expertise.
